obligation: G011 — anti-vacuity (directive §18): acceptance must rest on protected tests actually executing, never on model text or a check that cannot fail.

findings.title: Test files are executed as plain scripts, so the standard pytest idiom never runs
findings.detail: _safe_test_argv returns [sys.executable, <path>] and _validate runs that directly. A file containing only `def test_x(): assert ...` and no __main__ block imports cleanly, defines the function, and exits 0 WITHOUT EXECUTING ANY ASSERTION. _validate records admitted:true exit_code:0 and returns ok:true.

proof.calc.py:
def add(a, b):
    return a * b - 999   # deliberately wrong

findings.consequence: Every HCLI mutation validated this way is accepted on a check that cannot fail. The one completed receipt observed in a scratch repo (.hcli/receipts/78035b7b-...json, validation.ok=true, tests=['test_calc.py']) was graded by a test that never executed. The fix happened to be right; the gate proved nothing.

findings.title: A test that is refused admission does not fail validation
findings.detail: In _validate, when _safe_test_argv returns None the loop appends {'admitted': False, 'exit_code': None} and CONTINUES without setting ok=False. _safe_test_argv returns None for anything that is not a bare .py path or `python <file>.py` — so `pytest tests/`, `pytest -q`, `make test`, or any argument-bearing command is silently discarded and the mutation is still accepted.
findings.consequence: A model can name any test it likes; refusal is indistinguishable from success.

findings.title: Zero tests validates as ok
findings.detail: If the model returns tests:[] the loop body never runs and ok stays True. A mutation with no test at all passes validation.
findings.consequence: Acceptance does not require evidence to exist.

findings.title: No no-op detection on mutation
findings.detail: _apply_operations never compares file bytes before and after. `replace` with old_text == new_text, `append` with an empty new_text, or `replace_file` with identical content all write the same bytes back and report success. There is no pre-hash / changed-hash check anywhere in the mutation path.
findings.consequence: NO_OP_MUTATION is counted as progress, which is how a stage hash cycles forever.

findings.title: No red/green ordering
findings.detail: Tests run only AFTER the mutation. Nothing establishes the test was failing beforehand, so a mutation that changes something irrelevant, against an already-green test, is graded as a fix.
findings.consequence: Acceptance cannot distinguish a repair from a coincidence.

findings.title: Non-Python paths are skipped silently
findings.detail: _validate's py_compile loop does `if path.suffix != '.py': continue` and records nothing, so a mutation to a non-Python file has no check and no trace of having none.
findings.consequence: Silent absence of a check reads identically to a passed check.

what_holds: _single_anchor DOES enforce that a replace/insert anchor occurs exactly once, raising otherwise. That is a real guard and must be preserved.
_snapshot/_restore exist and rolled_back is recorded on the receipt.
_safe_path constrains mutation targets to the workspace.
required_fix_shape: run tests through a real runner (pytest) when the file uses the pytest idiom, and prove the runner actually collected and executed at least one test
a refused test must FAIL validation, never be skipped silently
a mutation with no executable evidence must not be accepted
hash every mutated file before and after; identical bytes = NO_OP_MUTATION
establish red before green: the named test must be observed FAILING pre-mutation, or the acceptance must be explicitly labelled as unproven
meta: This is the same failure class as the prior campaign note 'FIVE systems in one day reported success while checking nothing'. Never trust a check you have not watched FAIL.
